title: India defend 209 to beat New Zealand by 22 runs and take ODI series 3-1
dek: Two days after being bowled out for 89, India's bowlers dismissed New Zealand for 187 at Mount Maunganui to seal India's first bilateral ODI series win in New Zealand in seven years.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India beat New Zealand by 22 runs in the fifth and final one-day international at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui, on Sunday, defending a modest 209 to win the series 3-1, two days after they were bowled out for 89 in a 244-run defeat in the fourth match.

Left-arm seamer Arshdeep Singh took three wickets for 30 runs in his 10 overs and was named player of the match. It is India's first bilateral ODI series win in New Zealand in seven years, and only their third ODI series win in the country, according to reports.

## How the match went

New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner won the toss and chose to bowl, and India's batting struggled again on a pitch that helped the seamers. The top order fell cheaply: Rohit Sharma made 7, Ruturaj Gaikwad 18 and Virat Kohli 5, according to reports. Ishan Kishan and Axar Patel rebuilt the innings with 46 each, and India were all out for 209 in 42.1 overs.

New Zealand never settled in reply. Arshdeep struck with the new ball and returned to take wickets later, Mohammed Siraj took two for 50 and Axar Patel two for 28, and the hosts were bowled out for 187 in 48.1 overs. Dean Foxcroft top-scored for New Zealand with 31. Reports differ slightly on the length of New Zealand's innings; the scorecard figure used here is 48.1 overs.

## What the captain said

India's captain, Shreyas Iyer, credited the bowlers. "It was a series for bowlers, not for batters. Everyone stood up to the occasion," he said after the match. He said the team had put the heavy defeat behind it quickly: "We forgot about the fourth ODI loss the next day." He said he had stuck with a plan built around the seamers and "wickets kept coming".

## The series

India won the first two matches and the third was abandoned because of rain, leaving them 2-0 up. New Zealand pulled one back in the fourth, also at Mount Maunganui, where Matt Henry took six wickets and India collapsed for 89. India had already won the T20 international series on the tour 3-2.

The result still leaves questions over India's batting. On Sunday the first three batters made 30 runs between them, and India did not pass 210 in either of the last two matches. The bowling, led by Arshdeep and Siraj, carried the series.

## What happens next

South Africa are India's next opponents, according to the captain, who said the team would have to adjust to very different conditions. Mr Iyer did not give dates for that series.
